tenancy_security_deposit.name: Tenant Security Deposit Disputes
tenancy_security_deposit.applicable_law: Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (Section 108) & State Rent Control Acts / Model Tenancy Act
key_principles: A landlord cannot arbitrarily deduct from a security deposit without providing itemized repair bills for damage beyond normal wear and tear.
Normal wear and tear (e.g., minor paint fading, routine aging) is the landlord's responsibility, not the tenant's.
Deposit must be returned within the notice period or 30 days of handing over vacant possession unless the lease deed specifies otherwise.
Remedies: (1) Written formal demand notice via registered post/email, (2) Approach Rent Authority / Rent Tribunal or Civil Court for summary recovery.
required_proof: Proof of security deposit payment (bank transaction receipt/UPI/cheque)
Move-in and move-out inspection photos/videos or handover email confirmation
Written communication (WhatsApp/Email) showing notice given and demand for refund
tenancy_security_deposit.escalation_threshold: If dispute exceeds ₹10 Lakhs, involves physical eviction threats, or forged lease agreements, a licensed High Court/District Court advocate is required.

consumer_e_commerce_refund.name: Consumer Goods & E-Commerce Refund / Defect
key_principles: Consumer Protection Act 2019 Section 2(7) protects anyone buying goods/services online or offline.
Unfair Trade Practice under Section 2(47): Refusing legitimate refund or delivering defective goods contrary to merchant terms.
Section 35: Filing complaint before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (DCDRC) for claims up to ₹50 Lakhs (e-Daakhil portal).
National Consumer Helpline (NCH - 1915 or consumerhelpline.gov.in) provides free pre-litigation grievance mediation.
required_proof: Photographs / unboxing video of damaged or wrong product
Chat transcripts or customer service ticket history
consumer_e_commerce_refund.escalation_threshold: Claims above ₹50 Lakhs, medical negligence causing injury, or commercial trade disputes require formal legal counsel.

unpaid_salary_employment.name: Unpaid Salary / End-of-Service Settlement
unpaid_salary_employment.applicable_law: Payment of Wages Act, 1936 & State Shops and Commercial Establishments Act
key_principles: Wages must be paid by the 7th or 10th of the succeeding month.
Full and final settlement (F&F) including unpaid salary, encashable leave, and bonus must generally be settled within 30–45 days of relieving.
An employer cannot arbitrarily withhold earned wages even if a dispute regarding notice period exists without formal inquiry.

Remedies: (1) Formal Legal Demand Notice giving 15 days, (2) Grievance to the Labour Commissioner under State Shops & Establishments Act, (3) NCLT insolvency application for corporate defaults exceeding statutory thresholds.
required_proof: Salary slips / Bank statement showing prior monthly credits
Resignation letter and written acceptance / Relieving email
unpaid_salary_employment.escalation_threshold: Workplace sexual harassment (POSH), criminal breach of trust (IPC/BNS), or executive disputes involving ESOPs require specialized labor attorneys.

forbidden_hallucinations: Never cite non-existent Supreme Court case citations (e.g. 'Ramesh v. State 2018').
Never cite criminal codes (BNS / IPC) for routine civil contract disputes.
Do not quote fake section numbers; only cite sections verified in this knowledge base.
